transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-16
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Noah (Redwood); Lena, Rahul, Sofia, Tomás (Fenris)

Summary:
Fenris is evaluating open models and deciding whether Hosted, Dedicated reserve capacity, or Private VPC makes sense. Key constraints: lots of long-context multi-turn customer support threads (many >20k tokens historically), bilingual Spanish/Portuguese + English, strict EU data residency for telemetry, SOC2/ISO audit requirements, and low latency for real-time suggestions. They want to understand tradeoffs (latency vs cost), model accuracy on domain finetuned prompts, and tool-calling support for a small set of internal APIs.

Topics: model selection (Llama2/MPT/GPT-like open models), context lengths (8k/32k/64k), multilingual behavior, function/tool calling and safe execution, deployment modes (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC), encryption/KMS and audit logs, benchmarking plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Redwood - Maya: hey everyone thanks for carving out the time uh we'll start, quick intros then jump into your context.
[00:12] Customer - Lena: hi all, lena here leads ai at Fenris. we've been prototyping on premise with a mix of small fine-tuned models but want to move to a production inference strategy. main asks: handle long support threads, spanish/pt support, and tool-calling to our ticketing API.
[00:26] Redwood - Ethan: great, thanks. quick q on volumes, rahul?
[00:30] Customer - Rahul: yeah, typical concurrency peaks about 150 rps of short chitchat but for the suggestion pipeline we burst to 600 requests an hour with sequences averaging 6k tokens, but about 10% of sessions go beyond 20k.
[00:45] Redwood - Noah: mm-hmm okay so you have heavy tail long-context needs — that maps to choices on models and runtime like kv cache and prefix caching. note our KV cache is K V cache in the runtime and can do automatic prefix eviction.
[00:58] Customer - Sofia: quick security point — we need to know about key management, is HSM supported for private deployments and do you provide audit logs that our compliance team can ingest?
[01:10] Redwood - Maya: yes, for Redwood Private we provide customer managed KMS/HSM integration and a detailed audit log stream; for Hosted we offer managed KMS and SOC two docs, but we know some enterprise customers require the full private control plane.
[01:24] Customer - Tomás: what's the main difference from Dedicated? why not just reserve a dedicate pool?
[01:30] Redwood - Ethan: good q — Dedicated is reserved capacity on our GPU fleet that gives predictable throughput and lower per-token cost for steady workloads. Private gives you the control plane in your VPC or on prem with customer network and sometimes HSM and airgap options. Hosted is fastest to start but less isolation. if data residency is a blocker — Private is typical.
[01:52] Customer - Lena: we are EU-first for customer data; we can send logs to our SIEM but need retention controls. also curious about quantization and model fidelity — will 4-bit quantized models still do our long-span co-reference well?
[02:05] Redwood - Noah: generally yes; quant profiles are model-dependent. we recommend running Redwood Optimize evals for your prompt-set. quantization helps cost but can introduce subtle regressions on long-range co-reference — we can run controlled evals during the POC.
[02:20] Customer - Rahul: can you support 64k? some of our archival threads could reach that, but maybe we can chunk?
[02:28] Redwood - Ethan: runtime supports up to 128k for particular model variants and hardware, but throughput/latency tradeoffs increase non-linearly. for most production we recommend 32k as sweet spot — easier to get consistent SLOs. for occasional 64k we use hybrid caching + on-disk KV spill.
[02:45] Customer - Lena: model choices — we're comparing Llama2 variants (13B/70B), MPT-30B, and some llama-derivative open checkpoints; want your view on accuracy vs cost for multilingual customer support.
[02:58] Redwood - Noah: for multilingual, model pretraining matters — Llama2-70B tends to be stronger but costlier; MPT-30B with some domain finetune and adapter stacks can be surprisingly good and more cost-efficient. our benchmark sheet will show per-token cost and hits on your eval prompts. also consider mixing models: smaller model for short-turn routing and a larger model for long/complex threads.
[03:20] Customer - Sofia: tool-calling — our ticketing API requires user-scoped auth and we want safe sandboxing. how does Redwood handle tool invocation and access control?
[03:32] Redwood - Maya: we support structured tool-calling (function calling) out of the box. for Hosted you can use token-scoped credentials that Redwood can inject via secure vaulting; in Private you keep the connections internal to VPC. we also have RBAC per-route so you can limit which model can call which tool.
[03:49] Customer - Tomás: any examples of sandboxing or policy enforcement?
[03:52] Redwood - Ethan: yes, we have pre-built hooks to run a validation lambda pre-call and allowlist patterns. also audit logs capture tool-call parameters (redacted as needed) for compliance.
[04:05] Customer - Lena: good. latency expectations — we want suggestions near-interactive (<200ms) for short prompts, but I realize long context changes that.
[04:14] Redwood - Noah: exactly — sub-200ms is achievable for small context on lower-parameter models in Dedicated with local GPU. For 8k/32k contexts you should expect 400-800ms depending on model and batching; 64k+ pushes latency higher. caching and prefix KV helps reduce repeated token decode.
[04:33] Customer - Rahul: how does batching impact latency vs cost? we have bursty traffic.
[04:38] Redwood - Ethan: batching reduces cost by increasing GPU utilization but increases tail latency if you enforce lower SLOs. Dedicated allows you to tune batch windows and autoscale rules; Hosted uses conservative defaults but you can request customized policies on enterprise tiers.
[04:55] Customer - Sofia: about credentials and SSO — is SAML/SAML2 supported? our corp uses SSO and we need role sync.
[05:03] Redwood - Maya: yes, SSO with SAML and OIDC integrations plus SCIM for user provisioning are supported. apologies if previous docs said semel — transcription issues, but yes SAML.
[05:18] Customer - Lena: any sharp surprises when moving from Hosted to Private? network egress, latency to your control plane, or data plane management?
[05:27] Redwood - Noah: Private requires more ops from your side: VPC setup, peering, and you'd host the control plane components — we provide IaC and runbooks. egress is controlled by your infra; latency to other Redwood services like model updates is handled via sync agents. we do offer a managed on-prem appliance for air-gapped environments.
[05:46] Customer - Rahul: curious about rollouts — can we do canary and automatic fallback to smaller models if latency spikes?
[05:52] Redwood - Ethan: yes, Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, model pinning, and automated fallback policies (e.g., route to a cheaper model variant or cached response on overload).
[06:05] Customer - Tomás: cost model — what should we expect per 1k prompts at 8k context vs 32k?
[06:12] Redwood - Maya: we'll share the TCO sheet but rough ballpark: for a mid-sized open 13B quantized on Dedicated you're looking X cents per 1k tokens; moving to 32k and 70B increases cost significantly — we'll detail this in the spreadsheet.
[06:24] Customer - Lena: okay, POC ask: run a 2-week POC with both Dedicated reserved pool and Hosted fallback; evaluate accuracy on a labeled set of 500 threads (spanish + english) and measure latency for 8k and 32k.
[06:38] Redwood - Maya: sounds good. for the POC we'll propose two configs: A) Dedicated reserved with burst, quant profiles; B) Hosted with model variants and private VPC for sensitive traffic. we'll include KV cache settings.
[06:51] Customer - Sofia: also include the compliance pack and confirm retention windows for logs in Hosted.
[06:58] Redwood - Ethan: noted. we'll confirm retention and redact options.
[07:04] Customer - Rahul: who will be our primary SE contact for benchmarks?
[07:07] Redwood - Maya: Ethan will own the bench runs, Noah will help with runtime config and quant profiles.
[07:12] Customer - Tomás: timeline — we want a pilot in January.
[07:15] Redwood - Maya: doable. we'll aim to have bench results and POC plan by Dec 23, pricing and contract basics by Dec 18.
[07:24] Customer - Lena: thanks all. can you also include some example prompts so we can see how tool-calling payloads look?
[07:29] Redwood - Noah: yes, we'll share tool-call examples and the safe-call middleware pattern.
[07:34] (brief cross talk, agreement)
[07:40] Redwood - Maya: recap — action items, send TCO and security docs, run bench on 8k/32k for shortlisted models, share POC plan and schedule demo of private control plane. next meeting: fenris + redwood demo w/ demo account — propose Dec 22 or 23.
[07:56] Customer - Sofia: prefer Dec 23 afternoon CET.
[07:59] Redwood - Maya: ok we'll follow up via calendar.
[08:02] Customer - Lena: thanks everyone, good session.

End transcript.
